Title: Brobots
Pitch_Text:
Trapped in a laboratory invaded by a crystalline virus, you and your teammate take control of 2 complementary extermination robots sent to eliminate the threat.

Brobots is a two-player cooperative Fast FPS. Its core concept can be summed up as: "Me and Bro Vs the world", with a strong emphasis placed on cooperation and facing the challenges of the world as a duo.
SumUp_Text:
Due to the size of our team, the organization of this project was very close to one of a small studio. It was my first first time working with two other programmers, bringing up the challenge of task distribution.

I was able to specialize in the design and implementation of our enemies' artificial intelligences as well as the creation of several development tools.

Project completed as part of my studies at Rubika Valenciennes
Realisation_Text:
As a programmer on Brobots, I was responsible for designing the enemy AIs as well as creating development tools. My contributions are the following:

• Enemy AI: The enemy script architecture uses a component-based "Decorator pattern", allowing us to create versatile scripts and enabling fast iteration while creating our enemies. Creating a new enemy becomes very simple: adding the main script ("EnemyCore") and the desired behavior scripts (movement, attacks, targeting, health) is enough to create a new enemy. With the same goal of improving iteration speed, I was particularly attentive to create clean and readable custom inspectors.
Furthermore, in a multiplayer game context, it is important that all enemy execution logic (both core scripts and behavior scripts) is processed on the server side and then dispatched to clients.

• Spawning system: Enemy spawners work using a system based on sub-arenas that continuously spawn enemies until the players use their special ability. The enemy spawn system is easily tweakable thanks to Scriptable Objects, exposing enemy spawn costs, spawn speed, and other parameters. The spawners also act as the connection between enemies and the pathfinding request system.

• Optimization: Pathfinding was an important aspect to monitor for optimization. Therefore, I quickly decided to implement a custom grid system to divide our levels into a grid. This allowed us to achieve more precise movement behaviors that would have been more complicated to implement using Unity's NavMesh. Then, whenever an enemy needs to update its path, it sends a request to a manager which ensures a more balanced distribution of requests across multiple frames. Once the request is accepted, the enemy searches for the closest grid node using a three-dimensional binary search tree initialized during Awake. A final optimization step was implemented in the A* algorithm, which cleverly uses Dictionaries, Sorted Sets, and Min Heap to reduce the cost of pathfinding calls.

• Visual integration: From the beginning of the project, I kept visual integration in mind. I made sure to separate my scripts into task scripts, which handle logic execution, and "Viewer" scripts, which listen to the task scripts and execute the visual logic (Animations, UI updates, VFX, SFX). This allowed me to speed up the integration while limiting the impact on my task scripts when visuals were not yet functional.

• Tools: During this project, I created two tools to facilitate development. The first one allows easy editing of the custom grid (see optimization). The second one speeds up Level Artists' workflow by allowing them to randomly place objects (from a list) by clicking in the scene (notably used for placing rocks on the ground).

• Event Bus : The event bus is a system to dissocitate our scripts from one another. It works by scriptssending events and others beeing subscribe to those events.
Amelioration_Text: Although the project went very well overall, I believe I still need to improve my communication within a team of this size. I quickly found myself working independently on my tasks without much communication with the game designers and game artists responsible for producing the enemies. However, I improved towards the end of the project by communicating more regularly with my team.
